old: This name for a spiky, edible flower bud made a five-language relay race before reaching English speakers.
Its Arabic ancestor, al-ḵuršūf, passed through Spanish and Occitan hands before an Italian dialect gave it the shape we recognize.
Lombard articioch is the direct source of this English word for a vegetable with a heart worth digging for.
clues: This garden vegetable's name began in Arabic and was reshaped by four more languages on its way to English.
It is the cultivated flower bud of a thistle, eaten leaf by leaf by scraping the tender bases with your teeth, saving the meaty heart for last.
Its hearts are sold marinated in jars, and it joins spinach in a warm, creamy, cheesy dip at parties.
